Classic Invert listing copy vs invert-colors engineering — two different jobs

Teams assume Classic Invert compatibility covers storefront language. iOS, UIAccessibility, and Connect actually separate in-app inversion handling from product-page copy:

  • Classic Invert on the device — system-wide full display inversion: UI chrome, photos, video, and media all invert together. Toggle under Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Classic Invert, or Display Accommodations → Invert Colors → Classic Invert depending on iOS version. System accessibility behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Invert-colors implementation in the app — UIAccessibilityInvertColors checks, asset variants for inverted displays, ensuring icons and custom UI remain readable when the entire screen inverts, and handling photos or video previews when Classic Invert is on. Engineering inside the binary — not listing rewrite.
  • Classic Invert marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app respects Classic Invert, works with Invert Colors, or stays readable when full display inversion is on. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Classic Invert support in the app.

A Classic Invert–compatible app and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe full display inversion on the store page, not whether inverted colors render correctly inside the app.

Classic Invert vs Smart Invert, Dark Mode, Color Filters, and Display Accommodations — disambiguation

Apple groups several display-adjustment toggles under Accessibility. Indie teams conflate them on one product page. AppLocale covers Classic Invert and full display inversion marketing on listing metadata — not the other features:

  • Classic Invert (this page) — inverts the entire display including photos, video, and media. Gallery frames may show Settings → Display & Text Size → Classic Invert toggles, before/after full-inversion comparisons, or "Respects Classic Invert" badges. zh-Hans terms: 经典反转, 经典反色, 反转颜色, 经典反转颜色.
  • Smart Invert (different) — inverts the UI but tries to leave images, photos, and video looking normal — 智能反转. Smart Invert is a separate setting with different screenshot framing and buyer vocabulary; do not reuse Classic Invert boilerplate for Smart Invert claims.
  • Dark Mode (different) — light and dark UI appearance theme switching — 深色模式. Dark Mode changes appearance palette; Classic Invert flips all on-screen colors including media. See Dark Mode listing guide — appearance themes are not invert-colors copy.
  • Color Filters / Color Tint / Grayscale (different) — tint or grayscale presets under Display Accommodations — 颜色滤镜. Color filters adjust hue or saturation; Classic Invert negates colors across the entire display. Do not conflate 颜色滤镜 with 经典反转 on listing copy.
  • Differentiate Without Color (different) — shape-based differentiation preset under Display Accommodations — 不用颜色区分. Not full display inversion marketing.
  • Display Accommodations hub (different) — umbrella page for color filters, smart invert, reduce white point, and related presets. See Display Accommodations listing guide when your English source markets the whole accommodations menu — not when Classic Invert alone is your lead claim.
  • Increase Contrast (different) — stronger UI element borders and fills — 增强对比度. See Increase Contrast listing guide — UI contrast boosts are not full-screen color inversion.
  • Reduce Transparency (different) — less blur and frosted glass — 降低透明度. See Reduce Transparency listing guide — opacity changes are not invert-colors copy.
  • On/Off Labels & Button Shapes (different) — switch labels and button outlines under Display & Text Size. See On/Off Labels listing guide — unrelated to display inversion.
  • Auto Brightness (different) — automatic display brightness under Display & Brightness — 自动亮度. Separate path from Classic Invert; do not conflate on listing copy.

Your gallery may show a Classic Invert toggle on one frame and a Dark Mode comparison on the next — but listing copy should name each claim accurately per frame. A full-inversion demo is not a Smart Invert media-preservation badge, not a Dark Mode theme switch, and not a color-filter picker unless that is what the screenshot shows.

What Classic Invert actually does — listing honesty

Apple ships Classic Invert in iOS and iPadOS Accessibility settings. When enabled, the system inverts everything on screen — interface chrome, photos, video, and embedded media — so light areas become dark and colors flip across the full display. This differs from Smart Invert, which tries to preserve normal-looking images. Third-party apps may complement Classic Invert with readable icons, contrast-safe custom UI, or media handling when inversion is on. AppLocale rewrites listing copy from what your US page already claims:

  • Separate Classic Invert from Smart Invert in copy — Classic Invert inverts photos and video; Smart Invert tries to leave media looking normal. Listing vocabulary must follow your English lead feature and gallery frames.

Classic Invert–specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Full-inversion marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Classic Invert — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Classic Invert vs generic "dark mode" or "high contrast"

US pages use "Respects Classic Invert", "Works with Invert Colors", or "Readable when Classic Invert is on." China storefront copy often uses 经典反转, 经典反色, 反转颜色, or 经典反转颜色 — depending on whether you mean Apple's Classic Invert setting specifically or general inversion-aware UI. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope, not inventing Classic Invert support your app does not ship.

Classic Invert vs Smart Invert — do not conflate

Classic Invert inverts the entire display including photos and video. Smart Invert inverts UI chrome but tries to leave media looking normal — 智能反转. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 智能反转 when your English source only markets full display inversion. If you support both behaviors accurately, say both; if you support Classic Invert only, keep Smart Invert vocabulary out of subtitle, keywords, and overlays.

Classic Invert vs Dark Mode — do not conflate

Dark Mode switches light and dark appearance themes — 深色模式. Classic Invert negates on-screen colors system-wide including media. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 深色模式 when your English source only shows invert-colors toggles. See the Dark Mode listing guide only if appearance themes are your lead marketing claim.

Classic Invert vs Color Filters and Grayscale

Color Filters apply tint or grayscale presets under Display Accommodations — 颜色滤镜. Classic Invert flips all colors across the display. When your gallery only shows Classic Invert toggles, keep color-filter vocabulary out of subtitle and keywords.

Settings path wording across iOS versions

Newer iOS versions surface Classic Invert under Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Classic Invert. Some versions nest it under Display Accommodations → Invert Colors → Classic Invert. zh-Hans copy can reference 经典反转 or 反转颜色 for the feature name without over-specifying menu depth unless your English gallery shows one path consistently.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need invert-colors search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 经典反转, 反转颜色, and 经典反色 each signal different intent from Smart Invert, Dark Mode, or Color Filter keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Respects Classic Invert" headlines on gallery frames showing Settings → Accessibility → Classic Invert — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

AppLocale FAQ

What is Apple Classic Invert and why does listing copy matter?

Classic Invert is under Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Classic Invert on newer iOS versions, or Display Accommodations → Invert Colors → Classic Invert on some versions. When enabled, iOS inverts the entire display including photos and video. Marketing that feature on your en-US page does not auto-fill zh-Hans Connect fields.

Does shipping Classic Invert support auto-translate my China listing?

No. Classic Invert compatibility is in-app UI and media handling — it does not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback on the product page.

How is this different from Smart Invert?

Classic Invert listing copy markets full display inversion including media — 经典反转. Smart Invert inverts UI but tries to leave photos and video looking normal — 智能反转. Each is a separate Apple setting — do not reuse boilerplate across them.

How is this different from Dark Mode, Color Filters, or Display Accommodations?

Dark Mode covers light/dark appearance themes — 深色模式. Color Filters cover tint and grayscale presets — 颜色滤镜. Display Accommodations hub copy covers multiple display-adjustment presets together.
